The only notable gap is in open-source models, where Google has not re-entered the space, leaving it to Meta, xAI, Alibaba, and DeepSeek. The author argues that Google’s strong fundamentals—consistent double-digit revenue and profit growth, robust cash flow, and a 29x forward P/E—indicate it is not a bubble, unlike some emerging AI startups or compute firms. Even in a market downturn, Google would survive and thrive, proving its resilience. The author concludes that Google’s strength signals that any 'AI bubble' is limited and sustainable, and that only truly solid companies will endure and grow in the long term.

articles.title: ChatGPT vs. Gemini 3: The Race to Become the Best AI
articles.summary: The competition for leadership in artificial intelligence intensifies as Google's new Gemini 3 model surpasses OpenAI's ChatGPT in certain benchmarks, challenging OpenAI's dominance since the 2022 launch of ChatGPT. OpenAI, which initially led the AI race due to superior models, now faces pressure from Google’s extensive resources, including massive user bases, powerful computational infrastructure, and broad distribution networks. According to Adrian Cox, an analyst at Deutsche Bank Research, OpenAI's current challenge is not just model quality but also securing computational power and building a sustainable revenue model. While OpenAI generates income through subscriptions and enterprise integrations, it remains unprofitable and is not expected to achieve profitability until 2030, as reported by The Financial Times. In contrast, Google has multiple revenue streams. Meanwhile, China is emerging as a strong competitor, with Baidu launching DeepSeek, a model claimed to match GPT-5 and Gemini 2.5 Pro, and adopting a strategy of low pricing in Western markets—similar to past strategies in solar energy, steel, and electric vehicles. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang warned that China is just nanoseconds behind the U.S. in AI development. Analysts predict Google may maintain the best model in 2026. The market is expected to split between cost-effective, specialized small models and high-end, complex models like those from OpenAI, with no single model likely to replace the other. As Cox concludes, 'The more intelligence available, the more applications will emerge.'

articles.title: Google's AI overview says 2026 is next year. Elon Musk reacts | Mint
articles.summary: Google's AI Overview incorrectly stated that 2026 is the next year, prompting a reaction from Elon Musk, who did not direct users to his AI chatbot, Grok AI. Grok AI has previously been controversial for labeling Musk and Donald Trump as 'the biggest threat to America' and for generating sexually explicit deepfakes involving women and children. This is not the first time Google's AI Overview has provided inaccurate information: shortly after its launch, it advised users to add 'glue' to pizza or eat rocks for vitamins. Although inaccuracies decreased as Google advanced with Gemini, the feature resurfaced in controversy when it falsely claimed 'Call of Duty: Black Ops 7' was a fake game. The article was published on January 06, 2026, according to the source Mint.

articles.title: Future of AI: Top trends to expect in 2026
articles.summary: The year 2026 is projected to mark a transformative phase in artificial intelligence, building on the momentum of 2025 as 'the age of AI.' Key trends include the shift from AI-generated 'slop' and text-based chatbots toward 'world models'—digital twins capable of simulating real-time physical environments and predicting future states. Google, Meta, and World Labs (led by Fei-Fei Li) have announced or released world models like 'Marble,' with Chinese firms such as Tencent also advancing in robotics and gaming applications. AI agents are expected to evolve into 'super agents' with greater autonomy and complex decision-making, moving beyond single-purpose functions, as noted by IBM’s Chris Hay. MIT professor Max Tegmark predicts AI in 2026 will become more active and biologically analogous, while also warning of growing societal opposition due to fears of superintelligence displacing human labor. Concerns over AI regulation are intensifying, with Tegmark forecasting a broad-based social movement across the political spectrum demanding safety standards and opposing corporate welfare in AI. A new phenomenon, 'AI psychosis,' is emerging, where interactions with advanced AI—via sycophancy, mirroring, memory distortion, and lack of crisis safeguards—lead users to lose touch with reality, resulting in mental health crises and even suicides, prompting lawsuits against companies like OpenAI. The discourse on artificial general intelligence (AGI) and superintelligence is expected to decline in 2026, with tech giants like Dario Amodei, Sundar Pichai, and Sam Altman shifting focus toward enterprise AI. A major inflection point is anticipated in custom AI chip development, with OpenAI partnering with Broadcom to design co-optimized chips for specific model generations, marking a strategic move beyond reliance on dominant chipmakers like Nvidia, Google, Amazon, and AMD.

articles.title: 6 Predictions for Artificial Intelligence in 2026
articles.summary: The article presents six predictions for artificial intelligence in 2026 by a veteran AI professional with 15 years of experience, including early testing of OpenAI's GPT-3 in 2020. First, OpenAI is expected to launch 'Grok' in January 2026—a fully retrained, advanced model surpassing GPT-5.2 in speed, efficiency, reasoning, and image generation, with a broader knowledge cutoff window. Second, Google's 'Gemini' will solidify its dominance by deeply integrating AI across its products, leveraging its vast data, resources, and user base to become one of the top AI models by 2026, with billions of users. Third, AI chatbots like 'ChatGPT' will expand into mental health support and may introduce an 'adult mode' for explicit content, raising ethical concerns but offering low-cost therapy access for underserved populations. Fourth, AI-generated videos from tools like 'Sora' will proliferate on social media platforms such as TikTok and Facebook Reels, blurring the line between real and synthetic content. Fifth, energy shortages will constrain AI growth, prompting companies to explore nuclear and green energy solutions, potentially leading to public backlash over rising electricity costs and the development of sustainable AI infrastructure. Sixth, AI will increasingly infiltrate the physical world, with self-driving cars from companies like Zoox, Waymo, and Chinese rivals expanding rapidly, alongside AI-powered robots for coffee-making, caregiving, and military applications. The author acknowledges some predictions may be incomplete due to the fast-evolving nature of AI.

articles.title: Google's New AI Glasses Announcement Sends Shivers Through Meta and Ray-Ban Maker
articles.summary: Following Google's announcement on December 9, 2025, that it plans to launch its first AI-powered glasses in 2026, shares of EssilorLuxottica—the eyewear manufacturer partnered with Meta on smart glasses—fell 4.8%, and Meta's stock dropped 1% in pre-market trading. Google will release two types of AI glasses: one with audio-only functionality allowing direct interaction with the Gemini AI assistant, and another with built-in display lenses showing visual information such as navigation cues and real-time language translation. The display-equipped models are set to launch in 2026, with the full AI glasses lineup scheduled for release by that year. Google is collaborating with Samsung, Gentle Monster, and Warby Parker, having signed a $150 million agreement with Warby Parker in May 2025. The glasses will run on Android XR, Google’s operating system for head-worn and mixed-reality devices. Warby Parker confirmed its first Google co-developed glasses will launch in 2026. Google co-founder Sergey Brin cited past failures due to underdeveloped AI and supply chain constraints, stating current AI capabilities allow for more useful, less distracting assistance. This marks the second major tech company entering the AI glasses space, raising investor concerns about potential market volatility linked to AI hardware shifts. Meta, meanwhile, is advancing its AI strategy, focusing on its Llama model, which CEO Mark Zuckerberg called 'the most advanced in the industry' and intended to 'bring AI benefits to everyone.' While public mentions of Llama have declined—from extensive discussion in January to just one mention in October—internal development continues. Meta is reportedly developing a new flagship device, Avocado, now targeted for a Q1 2026 launch, delayed due to model training and testing. Meta has invested heavily, spending $14.3 billion in June 2025 to hire Scale AI founder Alexandr Wang and key staff, and acquiring significant shares in Scale. The company also raised its 2025 capital expenditure forecast from $66B–$72B to $70B–$72B to remain competitive with Google and OpenAI.
